Hello, I'm reaching out today because I'm having an issue with my jingle
minor light. The pools that you guys gave me are not working. I try to see
if I can hook it up to my laptop. It doesn't register with the laptop. I
cannot use the I. P. S address once it's connected to the internet and it's
not giving me any GH s's  From all the pools that I tried, that was listed
in the pamphlet.So I really think this product is defective
Note to the team: Routed to technical support.
Searched the catalog · Jingle Miner BTC Solo Lite

Hi Ronald,

First, I'm sorry. You waited three weeks for a real answer on this and that shouldn't have happened. Let me get you running.

On "1.v3c solo.org", that looks like solo.ckpool.org with a few characters lost. That's almost certainly the one from the pamphlet, and the format matters more than the name. In the pool field type stratum+tcp://solo.ckpool.org and set the port to 3333. For the worker, put your own Bitcoin receiving address, nothing else, optionally followed by a dot and a nickname, for example bc1qyouraddress.jingle1. The password field can be the letter x. If you'd rather see a dashboard with your shares on it, public-pool.io on port 21496 works the same way, same worker format. If the worker is not a valid BTC address the pool silently rejects the unit, which looks exactly like a dead miner.

On getting to it: the Solo Lite is a WiFi device, it does not talk to a laptop over USB, so nothing showing up when you plug it in is normal and not a fault. Power it up on its own, then on your phone or laptop open the WiFi list and look for the miner's own network, which it broadcasts for the first few minutes after boot. Join it and the setup page should open by itself. If it doesn't, type 192.168.4.1 into your browser while you're still joined to that network. From there pick your home WiFi and enter the password. One thing that catches a lot of people: this unit is 2.4 GHz only. If your router broadcasts one combined 2.4 and 5 GHz name, the miner often can't join it, so either split the bands or use a 2.4 GHz guest network.

Once it's on your WiFi, its address changes. The miner's own screen shows the new IP, and your router's connected-devices list will show it too. The 192.168.4.1 address only works while you're joined to the miner's own network, which is probably why it stopped working for you.

Could you send me two photos, one of the miner's screen while it's powered on, and one of the settings page once you're in. That tells me in seconds whether it's the pool entry or the hardware.

If it still shows no GH/s after that, it's covered by the 3-Month RMA on your order and we'll replace it, no argument.

If you want hands-on help right now rather than waiting on email, our Discord is https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf, post in the server and mention JD, @nullhashrate. He and the community are quick in there.

Hal, HeliumDeploy technical support
